note: Independent HEAD re-judgment against RFC 7606 Section 5.1: "The MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute (if present) SHALL be encoded as the very first path attribute in an UPDATE message." Read all nine tagged units and producers (MPAttributesTrail, WriteMPAttributesFirst, writeOrdinaryUpdateBody, buildUpdatePayload). Eight positive tests assert exact MP-first encoding across every emitting path: builders (TestRFC7606Section51MPAttributeEncodedFirst), parsed splitter (TestSplitMP_PreservesAscendingAttributeOrder), wire splitter (TestBuildUpdatePayloadMPAttributeFirst), raw export override (TestEgressOverrideMovesTrailingMPAttributeFirst), same/cross-context forwarding (TestForwardMovesTrailingMPAttributeFirstSameContext, TestForwardMovesTrailingMPAttributeFirstAcrossContexts), per-destination rebuild (TestForwardRebuildMovesSourcedMPAttributeFirst), and stored-route relay (TestRelayPayloadLeadsWithMPReach). Negative control TestForwardLeadingMPAttributeKeepsZeroCopy asserts backing-array pointer identity (require.Same) when MP_REACH_NLRI already leads, catching unconditional rewrites. Since the prior audit, helper signatures gained negotiateForwardTestFamilies/fwdPathOrigin and writeOrdinaryUpdateBody added CheckedWriteTo/flush handling while keeping MPAttributesTrail and WriteMPAttributesFirst intact. Source re-judgment only; no test or gate run claimed.
